content:
mary: quick q — after rotating the imagePullSecret in vault we saw a flurry of Argo sync failures for the payment service. PRs from Atlantis apply seem to update k8s secret object but pods still fail with ImagePullBackOff. anyone seen this pattern?
aj: hm, do you mean the secret name changed or the secret data was replaced in-place?
mary: replaced in-place (same k8s secret name, new dockerconfigjson). Atlantis applied the terraform change that writes to k8s via provider + kubernetes_secret resource. argo shows sync failed: image pull auth.
lee: did the secret get propagated to the cluster argocd watches? sometimes argocd's repo state vs live diverges if secret is annotated/managed outside of git. any annotations like "argocd.argoproj.io/refresh": some-value?
mary: no argocd annotations. we rely on terraform managing the secret directly (we have a k8s provider in infra account).
aj: could be timing: GH Actions -> Atlantis apply -> terraform updates secret -> k8s object updated but nodes still have old credentials cached (container runtime). imagePull should re-evaluate on pod restart, though. are pods being restarted?
mary: pods restarted as part of deployment update a few mins later, but still get auth error. logs from kubelet: "Failed to pull image: unauthorized: authentication required". docker registry logs show rejected token exchange.
lee: check the secret's type and key name: it needs to be type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson and key .dockerconfigjson. if the provider wrote base64 data to a different key name we can get that error.
mary: verified type = kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, key = .dockerconfigjson, encoded looks valid.
aj: two other angles — 1) multi-cluster: are we writing to the control cluster but pods scheduled on a different cluster/namespace mapping? 2) imagePullSecrets referenced by ServiceAccount vs Pod spec? If SA references an old secret name or has immutable mount behavior?
mary: single cluster. pods reference imagePullSecrets: - name: reg-creds (same name as secret). ServiceAccount doesn't reference it.
lee: did you check dockerconfigjson content: registry URL hostnames must match image ref. If token is for registry.example.com but images use registry.internal.example.com (CNAME) auth may fail.
mary: good point. images use ghcr.io/redwood-inc/payment-service:prod. secret's auth host is ghcr.io. matches.
lee: another suspect — registry rate limits / token cache. If the registry invalidated the token right after rotation (race), older node kubelets might be fetching with stale creds cached in docker credential helper. Restarting kubelet or evicting pods should force re-pull.
aj: can you try restarting one node's kubelet or cordon+drain+uncordon a single node to force fully new pulls? maybe do a canary on one instance.
mary: planning to cordon+drain one node in staging now and recreate pods. testing on staging first.
deploy-bot: [deploy] terraform apply completed for branch mary/rotate-imagepull-2024 — 1 changed, 0 added, 0 destroyed (timestamp 1712345690)
lee: also check if imagePullSecrets are in the pod's spec after the rollout. Argo sometimes reverts parts of the spec if the manifest comes from git and secret is managed out-of-band. If the pod template in the deployment lacks imagePullSecrets it won't pick it up even if the secret exists.
mary: confirmed deployment spec includes imagePullSecrets. The rollout created new ReplicaSet with right pod template.
aj: can you paste the output of `kubectl get secret reg-creds -o yaml` (redact token) and `kubectl describe pod <failing-pod>`? maybe kubelet logs around the pull time too.
mary: paste below (redacting token):
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: reg-creds
  namespace: payments
type: kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson
data:
  .dockerconfigjson: REDACTED_BASE64
```
`kubectl describe pod payment-5c6f7c9d-xyz`:
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  2m ago  default-scheduler
  Normal  Pulled     1m ago  kubelet, ip-10-0-2-45  Successfully pulled image registry-auth-failed? wait — shows ImagePullBackOff now
  Warning BackOff   30s ago  kubelet, ip-10-0-2-45  Back-off pulling image "ghcr.io/redwood-inc/payment-service:prod"
  Warning Failed    30s ago  kubelet, ip-10-0-2-45  Failed to pull image "ghcr.io/redwood-inc/payment-service:prod": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to fetch anonymous token: unexpected status: 401
```
lee: that anonymous token msg is interesting — indicates docker client tried anonymous flow rather than using the secret. That suggests imagePullSecret wasn't mounted or used for that pull. Could be because the pod's service account has automountServiceAccountToken: false? Not relevant. More likely: node's containerd/docker config didn't receive the secret for that namespace?
aj: check `kubectl get pods -o yaml` and inspect `imagePullSecrets` present on pod manifest. Also run `kubectl get sa default -o yaml` to see if pod gets imagePullSecrets via SA.
mary: running checks...
(oncall-sre): if reproducing, try creating a pod with `imagePullSecrets` referencing reg-creds and run `kubectl run tmp --image=ghcr.io/redwood-inc/payment-service:prod --restart=Never --image-pull-policy=Always --overrides='{ "spec": { "imagePullSecrets": [{"name": "reg-creds"}]}}'` and see if it pulls. that isolates whether kubelet can use the secret.
mary: tried that, same ImagePullBackOff on a fresh pod. so node isn't using the secret for some reason.
lee: what container runtime on nodes? containerd? docker? certain runtimes expect secrets to be available to the kubelet credential provider. check node kubelet version and `kubectl describe node` for potential taints preventing secret sync.
mary: nodes are kubelet v1.28 + containerd 1.7. I'll check kubelet logs.
(oncall-sre): also check kube-apiserver admission: the secret lives in namespace payments; ensure RBAC isn't preventing the kubelet from reading secret (kubelet uses service account token to get imagePullSecret)? usually node has system:node role. unlikely.
mary: found root cause — terraform applied the secret but the kubernetes provider was pointed at the control-plane cluster context (where the secret was created) while the nodes are in the spoke cluster (different k8s API endpoint). basically wrong provider alias in the module. we had the secret in cluster-a but pods scheduled on cluster-b. argo was watching cluster-b and the secret was missing -> anonymous pull.
aj: ouch. glad it's staging. fix: update terraform k8s provider alias to use the spoke cluster creds for that namespace, or centralize secret propagation via sealed-secrets/gitops.
mary: pushing a fix to use correct provider alias + running `terraform apply` targeting the spoke provider. will also add a check in the module to assert provider alias equals var.target_cluster.
lee: can you add a small integration test in CI: create secret via terraform on cluster, then run `kubectl get secret` in that cluster to validate presence? could be an optional step in GH Actions for infra changes.
aj: we already have a GH Action job for terraform plan/apply. add a post-apply smoke test job that runs `kubectl --context=${TARGET} get secret ${SECRET_NAME} -n ${NS}` and fails build if missing. cheap guard.
mary: thanks. will do both changes.
deploy-bot: [note] created issue INFRA-523: add post-apply k8s smoke tests for secret propagation.
aj: once fixed, you might want to flush node credential caches or restart container runtime on nodes in prod if this ever happens there. but since we write to correct cluster it shouldn't recur.
mary: thanks everyone :thumbsup: will follow up once deployment green on staging and open PR for the smoke test.
lee: lgtm, and add a small doc in infra README about verifying target provider alias when modules manage cluster-local resources.
mary: adding doc now. done.
